Polyglott. a) Pet. a Fig. b) Mercer. prædicationem verbi, quo cognita illis redditur via salutis & liberationis,atque monentur ut ei insistant,id quod multi non faciunt juxta effatum: multi sunt Vocati, pauci electi, Matth. 20,16. (2.) Strictiori notione sumitur pro peculiari quadam vocatione, cui inest simul efficacia in eos operandi,qui ea sunt vocati,ut verbo auscultent ac obediant,atque eam ineant viam, quam illis exhibet ad consequendum promissam liberationem. Quod ad primam notionem attinet, ea non videtur hic accipi, quia cumprimis restringitur ad illos electos reliduos,qui liberationem inventuri erant: atque hi cum non sint alii, quam quos Deus erat vocaturus,necessario sequitur,omnes illos,quos Deus vocat vel vocaturus erat, esse reliduos. c) Eosdem S. Paulus innuit hac expressione, qui vocati sunt κατὰ πρόθεσιν, juxta propositum (vel ut nostrates habent, d) juxta suum propositum.) Rom. 8, 28. quos quoque dicit, Deum præcognoscere, prædestinare, vocare, justificare atque glorificare v. 29.30. Unde manifesto appareret,verbum Vocandi hic quid magis inferre atque includere,quam communem vocationem,nempe præcedentem e) electionem atque talem vocationem præstituto tempore,quæ ex gratia ejus in eos collata adeo efficax reddetur, ut eos Deo proprios vindicet ac ei obedientes reddat,quod omne Hazmanah præparatio, pulchre complectitur,& exquisite mihi hic videntur verborum sensum exprimere illi, qui exponunt: f) traxerit ad se, juxta illud quod dictum est a Salvatore nostro: Nemo potest ad me venire, nisi Pater, qui me misit, eum trahat, Joh. 6,44.
units.tr: u) Glassius, Grammar, p. 415, or in the margin at p. 653. 66) Pet. a Fig. Munster. x) LXX. Syr. y) So also the Arabic manuscript. z) In the Polyglot Bible. a) Pet. a Fig. b) Mercer. the preaching of the Word, by which the way of salvation and liberation is made known to them, and they are urged to walk in it; a thing that many do not do, according to the saying: many are called, but few are chosen, Matt. 20,16. (2) In a stricter sense it is taken for a particular calling, which at the same time has efficacy to work in those who are so called, so that they listen to the Word and obey it, and enter upon the way that it shows them for attaining the promised liberation. As for the first sense, it does not seem to be meant here, because it is especially restricted to those chosen remnant who are to find liberation; and since these are none other than those whom God was to call, it necessarily follows that all those whom God calls, or was to call, are the remnant. S. Paul points to these same people with the expression called according to purpose [κατὰ πρόθεσιν, kata prothesin, juxta propositum] (or, as our people have it, according to his purpose) Rom. 8, 28. whom he also says God foreknew, predestined, called, justified and glorified, vv. 29, 30. From this it clearly appears that the verb to call here implies and includes something more than the common calling, namely the preceding election and that calling at the appointed time, which by God's grace bestowed upon them becomes so effective that it claims them as God's own and makes them obedient to him. All this the word hazmanah, preparation, beautifully embraces; and those who explain it as has drawn to himself seem to me to express the sense of the words exactly, in accordance with what our Saviour said: No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, John 6,44.

units.la: Hac illorum descriptione, qui vocantur illi reliduI, quibus liberatio est futura, quia soli sunt, quos DEus vocabit,excludere videtur ex selecto hoc numero omnes illos g) hypocriticos simulatores,qui se tales venditant, cum non probent ita se esse ordinatos ad vitam recte ejus nomen invocando ac digne eo ambulando. Eadem opera ostenditur salutem illorum non esse ex propriis ipsorum viribus,operibus vel meritis,sed ex libera gratia Dei,quemadmodum S. Paulus eos vocat reliquias juxta electionem gratiæ, & si per gratiam, ergo non per
units.tr: By this description of those who are called the remnant, to whom liberation is to come, since they alone are those whom God will call, it seems that all those hypocritical pretenders are excluded from this chosen number, who put on a show of being such, though they do not prove that they are so ordered to live rightly by calling upon his name and walking worthily before him. At the same time it is shown that their salvation is not from their own powers, works or merits, but from the free grace of God; just as S. Paul calls them a remnant according to the election of grace, and if by grace, then not by

units.la: {e} Drusius. {d} Quamvis secus sentiat Hamm ondus omittens τὸ suum. {e} Calv. {f} Vatab. {g} Calv. Gvalt. per opera, Rom.11,5.6. Gratia seruati estis per fidem, idque non ex vobis, Dei donum est, non ex operibus, ne quis se iactet, Ephes.2.v.8.9.
units.tr: {e} Drusius. {d} Although Hammond thinks otherwise, omitting the word suum. {e} Calvin. {f} Vatablus. {g} Calvin, Gualther. works, Rom. 11,5.6. By grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God; not of works, lest anyone should boast, Eph. 2,8.9.

units.la: Praeter hanc significationem vocandi aliam etiam habet verbum קרא nimirum legendi, quam optime huic loco convenire putat Arias Montanus, ut verba sic habeant: quos Dominus legit, nempe in libro vitae, ubi sunt scripti, non deleti; sensus autem talis esset, plures quidem, imo omnes in eo fuisse inscriptos, attamen a multis commissum esse, ut eorum nomina de libro illo delerentur, hinc eos tantum reliduos, quos Dominus esset lecturus & non deleturus, liberationem esse inventuros. Quam notionem ut palam fieret satis esse commodam huic rei, ex aliis locis conatur probare, ubi ejusmodi expressiones adhibentur, veluti Exod.32,33. ubi Dominus dicit: cum qui peccaverit mihi, delebo de libro meo, unde ex eo, quod quidam dicantur delendi, apparet alios dici posse reliquos, qui legantur. Praeter alia loca N. Testamenti ab eo citata, ut Apoc.3,5. & 22,19. quae acceptionem vocis significatione legendi videntur confirmare, quibus addi potest Phil.4,3. sunt & alia duo V. Testamenti, quae Abarbinel allegat, huic rei maxime congruentia, ut Esa.4,3. Erit enim, ut qui reliquus fuerit in Zion & reliquus Hierosolymae, sanctus dicatur, quisquis adscriptus fuerit viventibus Hierosolymae; & Dan.12,1. Erit tempus angustiae, qualis non extitit, ex quo fuit gens usque ad tempus illud, & tempore illo liberabitur populus meus, quisquis inventus fuerit in libro illo.
units.tr: Besides this sense of calling, the verb קרא has another meaning, namely to read, which Arias Montanus thinks fits this passage very well, so that the words read: whom the LORD reads, namely in the book of life, where they are written and not blotted out. The sense would then be that many, indeed all, were written in it, but that many had committed things by which their names were to be blotted out of that book; hence only those of the remnant whom the Lord was going to read and not blot out would find liberation. To make this notion clear, he tries to prove that it is quite suitable to this matter from other passages where such expressions are used, such as Exod. 32,33., where the Lord says: whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book; whence, from the fact that some are said to be blotted out, it appears that others can be said to be remaining who are read. Besides other passages of the New Testament he cites, such as Rev. 3,5. & 22,19., which seem to confirm the acceptance of the word in the sense of reading, to which may be added Phil. 4,3., there are also two other passages of the Old Testament which Abarbanel cites as most congruous with this matter, namely Isa. 4,3.: He who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem; and Dan. 12,1.: There will be a time of distress such as has not been since there was a nation until that time; and at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in that book.

units.la: Qua ratione autem haec loquendi forma, voce legendi notione accepta, ex his locis citatis illustretur, res est per se manifesta. Etenim quo modo hi dicuntur in libro Dei vel vitae esse scripti, eodem etiam possunt dici lecti humano scilicet more loquendo de rebus divinis, uti homines sua agere vel de suis inter se loqui consueverunt. Ea enim est conditio illorum hominum, qui honorum vel privilegiorum quorundam causa scripti sunt in libro, ut publice legantur: quamdiu ita relinquuntur scripti, ad eos hi honores & privilegia pertinent; at si ex eo delentur, indicio est se illis privari, nec diutius esse iis fruituros. Ita ut libere ac sponte fluat sensus verborum, si redditur notione legendi; verum non nascitur alius nec est distinctus ab eo, quem nobis praebet significatio vocandi (quae generalis est, nec subest ulla ratio ab ea discedendi) quippe utrobique innuitur,illos, de quibus sermo est, a Deo esse electos & destinatos ad salutem,liberatumque iri, cum e contrario alii sint perituri. Praeterea ad liberationem praedictam utroque modo etiam referri potest, five eam intelligas ab omnibus ultimi diei malis, quae genuina quidem videtur hujus loci mens, five ab illis calamitatibus ac destructione,qua tota natio vel populus hic descriptus obruendus erat, ut alii,prout vidimus, hoc accipiunt.
units.tr: Now, how this way of speaking, taking the word in the sense of being read, is illustrated from the passages cited, is clear in itself. For just as those who are said in the book of God or of life to be written can also be called read (speaking in the human manner about divine things, as men are accustomed to speak of their own affairs and among themselves), so the condition of those men is this: those who are written in a book for the sake of certain honours or privileges are read out publicly. As long as they remain written there, these honours and privileges belong to them; but if they are erased from it, that is a sign that they are deprived of those things and will no longer enjoy them for long. So the sense of the words flows freely and naturally if it is rendered by the notion of being read; yet it does not arise as something different from, or distinct from, the meaning that calling gives us (which is general, and there is no reason to depart from it). Indeed, in both senses it is implied that those of whom the text speaks have been chosen and destined by God for salvation and will be delivered, while on the contrary others will perish. Moreover, the deliverance foretold can be referred to in either way, whether you understand it as deliverance from all the evils of the last day (which seems to be the genuine meaning of this passage) or from those calamities and that destruction by which the whole nation or people described here was to be overwhelmed, as others, as we have seen, understand it.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAP. III.

units.la: UT omnem hinc rerum turbationem ac confusionem procul ablegemus ac praeveniamus, quae fortean oriri posset in hoc capite exponendo, initio quidem praemittere confultum duxi magnam hic esse inter interpretes differentiam, cum de tempore, tum de personis, de quibus hic Propheta loquitur, uti ex parte jam vidimus ex v.31. praecedentis capitis, cujus ultima pars tam arcte cohaeret & conjuncta est cum his verbis, ut alii novum constituant caput a versu, qui juxta communem divisionem vigesimus octavus est. Ut autem hujus rei initium faciamus ab eo, quod Judaei de isto negotio statuunt, Aben-Ezra dicit multos eorum existimare hanc prophetiam esse לעתיד in futurum adjiciendo אולי כן היאה forsan ita efl; R. Moses autem id referre ad tempus Jehoshaphat & eam historiam, quae memoratur 2. Par. 20. de magna clade Ammonitarum & Moabitarum & Montanorum Seiris, qui cum contra Judaam effent pugnaturi, in se ipsos, Domino ita ordinante, arma stringerent, alterq; alterum perderet. Quo factum est, ut Jehoshaphat ejusque populus se congregarent in vallem Beracha sive benedictionis DEI, ut benedicerent Domino propter tam ingentem victoriam, a qua locus vocabatur vallis B.racha, (i. e, benedictionis) atque consimili modo ab eo, quod a Jehoshaphat hic factum erat, convallis Jehoshaphati, quo tempore
units.tr: So that we may drive away and forestall all confusion and disorder that might perhaps arise in expounding this chapter, I have thought it advisable to set out at the start that there is great disagreement among the interpreters, both about the time and about the persons of whom the Prophet here speaks, as we have already partly seen from verse 31 of the preceding chapter, whose last part coheres so closely and is so joined with these words that others make a new chapter beginning at the verse which, by the common division, is the twenty-eighth. But to begin this matter with what the Jews determine about this business: Aben-Ezra says that many of them think this prophecy refers to the future, adding אולי כן היאה [forsan ita erit, perhaps it will be so]. R. Moses, however, refers it to the time of Jehoshaphat and to that history which is recorded in 2 Chronicles 20, about the great slaughter of the Ammonites and Moabites and the mountain-dwellers of Seir, who, when they were about to fight against Judah, drew their weapons against one another, the Lord so ordaining, so that one destroyed the other. As a result, Jehoshaphat and his people gathered in the valley of Berachah, that is, of the blessing of God, to bless the Lord for so great a victory; from which the place was called the valley of Berachah (that is, of blessing), and in a similar way, from what Jehoshaphat did there, the valley of Jehoshaphat, at which time

units.la: etiam putant esse reversos, qui in captivitatem erant abducti temporibus patrum suorum. Ita Aben-Ezra ex R. Mose. Verum h) quod hoc minus sit probabile, ut alias rationes jam praetermittam, ex eo apparet quod id maxime videatur factum, antequam a Propheta hoc dictum sit, i) qui nobis non refert rerum praeteritarum historiam, sed praedicit futura. Sunt k) qui ad hanc historiam putant Prophetam alludere, ut illustret quae DEus postea esset facturus comparatione illorum, quae jam fecerat.
units.tr: they also think that those who had been led away into captivity in the times of their fathers returned. So Aben-Ezra, following R. Moses. But h) that this is less probable, to pass over other reasons, appears from the fact that it seems chiefly to have happened before this was spoken by the Prophet, i) who does not relate to us the history of past things but foretells future things. There are k) some who think the Prophet alludes to this history in order to illustrate what God was afterwards going to do by comparison with what he had already done.

units.la: Kimchi ad dies Messiae eam refert & ad bellum Gog & Magog, quod in valle Jehoshaphat prope Hierosolymam futurum sit. Ad idem tempus atque acta videtur hoc etiam referre R. Tanchum, ut vidimus ad v.31. praecedentis capitis; at quam parum certitudinis habeat, ex ejus ipsius apparet verbis, quibus finem imponit sententiae suae, quam expromsit de Gog & Magog in notis ad Ezech. 38. cujus verba apud Maimonid. citata (yad c. ult.) ita habent هـذه الامـور ومـا يشـبهها ليس بـيد الـعلـمـاء فيـهـا نـقـل محـقـق وانـما تـكـلم فيـهـا كل مـن تكـلم بحـسب مـا يـظـهـر مـن ظـواهـر النـصـوص وكـلـمـا ظـهـر مـنهـا شـيء انـكـشف الاخـبـار عـلـى حـقـيـقـتـهـا
units.tr: Kimchi refers it to the days of the Messiah and to the war of Gog and Magog, which is to take place in the valley of Jehoshaphat near Jerusalem. R. Tanchum seems to refer this also to the same time and events, as we saw at verse 31 of the preceding chapter; but how little certainty it has appears from his own words, with which he ends his opinion, which he expressed about Gog and Magog in his notes on Ezekiel 38, whose words, cited in Maimonides (Yad, last chapter), read thus: hadhihi al-umur wa ma yushbihuha laysa bi-yadi al-ulama fiha naql muhaqqaq, wa-innama takallama fiha kull man takallama bi-hasab ma yazhar min zawahir al-nusus; wa-kullama zahara minha shay' inkashafa al-akhbar 'ala haqiqatiha [Concerning these matters and such like, there is no certain tradition in the hands of the learned men; rather, whoever speaks of them speaks according to what appears from the outward sense of the texts, and whenever something of them appears, the reports are uncovered as to their reality].

units.la: i. e. Quod ad has res & harum similes, non est ulla certa traditio in manibus doctorum virorum, sed quicunque aliquid de illis dicit, ex eo dicit quod apparet ex vi verborum Textus (vel quo verba textus maxime videntur inclinare) & ubicunque tale quid apparet (actu), tunc revelatum est (vel manifestum redditum) quod de eo dictum est, juxta verum ejus sensum.
units.tr: That is: concerning these things and such like, there is no certain tradition in the hands of learned men, but whoever says anything about them says it from what appears from the force of the words of the text (or to which the words of the text seem chiefly to incline); and wherever something of this kind actually appears, then what was said of it is revealed (or made manifest) according to its true sense.

units.la: Alia ratione hoc exponit Abarbinel, quamvis caeteris consentit, ad Gog & Magog hic respici. Etenim existimat cum in his verbis, tum in praecedentibus (c.2,30.31.) rationem haberi Christianorum, quos
units.tr: Abarbinel expounds it in another way, although he agrees with the others that Gog and Magog is meant here. For he thinks that both in these words and in the preceding ones (ch. 2:30, 31) account is taken of the Christians, whom

units.la: h) Joelem enim tempore Jehoshaphat vixisse fallax conjectura est Aben-Ezrae ex opinione tantum illius R. Mosis nata. Recentiorem fuisse multi statuunt. i) Christ. a Castr. Druf. k) Merc. Pisc. vocat Edom (sub nomine solis depictos) & Mahomedanos, quos vocat Ismael (sub nomine lunæ) quibus utrisque non tantum cum Judæis non conveniat, sed ne quidem inter semetipsos; quippe qui multum contenderint de possessione terræ sanctæ, multaque bella & extra & circa illam gesserint, nunc hac parte eam aliquot annis occupante, nunc illa, donec utraque Judæos plane ea expulerint, atque hanc prophetiam innuere, DEum tempore hic prædicto acerrime esse vindicaturum maleficia utriusque in Judæos admissa. Cæterum his verbis expresse arbitratur prædictum esse, quamvis Mahomedani jam eam teneant, Christianos tamen iterum eandem esse invasuros atque magna clade Mahumedanos fusuros, quo tempore quidem futurum, ut Mahumedani Babyloniis, Assyriis & cæteris ex tractibus l) orientalibus conjuncti bello Christianis illato fusum fratrum suorum ulcisceretur sanguinem, sanctamque terram recuperarent; at tum DEus vindictam sumturum esse de Christianis æque ac de Mahomedanis, quia in propria sua viscera essent sævituri aliique alios fusuri. Et quoniam sanctam terram destruebant prima vice Assyrii & Babylonii, secunda Christiani, ideo a DEO etiam esse constitutum, ut eo ipso loco, quo istud nefas ab illis erat admissum, in eos severe animadverteretur; ubi probabile ipsi videtur, Gog tunc orientalium fore imperatorem & ducem. Non quod ipsi esset propositum adversus Israelem bellare, quæ est nonnullorum opinio, sed adversus Christianos illorum hostes, &, ratione DEI incitantis istum populum (id faciendum) a Propheta dictum esse putat: Congregabo omnes nationes &c. Ita ille suam ipsius profert opinionem, quam ipse fatetur sibi peculiarem esse & a cæteris in eo discrepantem: attamen pro se maxime facere autumat m) verba. Quid habeant veri, tempori commendandum est; interim constat nihil illis inesse certitudinis, parum probabilitatis. Atque hæ sunt Judæorum præcipuæ sententiæ de hujus Prophetiæ fine ac scopo; multo major est diversitas super hac re inter Christianos.
units.tr: h) The conjecture of Aben-Ezra that Joel lived in the time of Jehoshaphat is false, arising only from the opinion of that R. Moses. Many hold that he was later. i) Christ. a Castr. Druf. k) Merc. Pisc. calls Edom (depicted under the name of the sun) and the Mahometans, whom he calls Ishmael (under the name of the moon), both of whom not only do not agree with the Jews, but not even among themselves; for they have contended much over the possession of the Holy Land and have waged many wars both outside it and around it, now one of them occupying it for some years, now the other, until both have plainly driven the Jews out of it. He takes this prophecy to hint that God at the time foretold will most fiercely avenge the wrongs committed by both against the Jews. Moreover, he judges that it is expressly foretold that, although the Mahometans already hold it, the Christians will again invade the same land and rout the Mahometans with great slaughter. At that time, indeed, it will come about that the Mahometans, joined with the Babylonians, Assyrians and others from the eastern l) regions, will wage war on the Christians and avenge the blood of their brothers shed, and recover the holy land; but then God will take vengeance on the Christians as well as on the Mahometans, because they will rage against their own bowels and some will slaughter others. And since the Assyrians and Babylonians devastated the holy land the first time, and the Christians the second time, therefore God has also decreed that in the very place where that wickedness was committed by them they should be severely punished; where it seems probable to him that Gog will then be the commander and leader of the eastern peoples. Not that it was his purpose to make war against Israel, which is the opinion of some, but against the Christians, their enemies; and he thinks the Prophet said, with God urging that people to do it: I will gather all nations, etc. Thus he puts forward his own opinion, which he admits is peculiar to himself and differs from the others in this; yet he claims that the words especially favour him. What truth these ideas have must be left to time; meanwhile it is clear that there is no certainty in them and little probability. And these are the chief Jewish opinions about the end and purpose of this prophecy; the diversity among Christians on this matter is far greater.

units.la: l) Anguli Orientis. m) הנה דברי הנביאות יורוני רוכוני יוזמר לי nos. n) Cyrillus ea implenda prædici arbitratur redeuntibus Judæis ex captivitate Babylonica Cyro permittente, quodque factum memoratur apud Esram & Nehemiam, huc referendum esse censet. Alii respici volunt ad id, quod futurum erat o) Assyriis & Chaldæis. Alii ad recentiora tempora, post Christi adventum p); plurimi vero ad ultima tempora, cum venerit ad judicandum in excidio mundi. Alii rursus, licet his non refragentur, tamen præcise ad ultimum judicium restringi nolunt, sed ad omnia tempora extendendum esse contendunt, post primum ejus adventum ad secundum usque, nec non ad illud quod futurum est q), ad totum evangelii tempus, quo ecclesiam suam tueri, ejusque hostes destruere promittit, cujus rei utut non pauca extent exempla in hoc mundo, tamen ultimo rerum die plura erunt atque manifestiora. Has opiniones Reverendo r) Diodato colligere placuit in notis suis super priora verba, quas omnes locum habere in his & sequentibus verbis putat. Atque hoc ex parte etiam figurate exponi posse volunt de vindicta divina, quam DEus sumebat de hostibus populi sui post liberationem ex captivitate Babylonica; at præcipue & spiritualiter referendum esse ad judicia, quæ Christus exercet in hostes ecclesiæ ab eo redemtæ, in specie autem spectare ad ultimam & generalem liberationem in adventu secundo. Quibus autem rationibus hi atque alii interpretes in diversum nimium quantum distracti nitantur, quidve statuendum sit de illorum diversis opinionibus, magis e re futurum esse censeo id adjicere, cum verba in specie eo ordine, quo habentur, inspecturi sumus, cui negotio jam nos DEO juvante accingimus hisce in genere præmissis.
units.tr: l) The Corners of the East. m) הנה דברי הנביאות יורוני רוכוני יוזמר לי [Behold, the words of the prophets instruct me, ...] n) Cyril thinks it was foretold to be fulfilled when the Jews returned from the Babylonian captivity, by the permission of Cyrus, and he judges that it should be referred to what is recorded as done in Ezra and Nehemiah. Others wish it to be taken as referring to what was to happen to the o) Assyrians and Chaldeans. Others refer it to later times, after the coming of Christ p); but most refer it to the last times, when he will come to judge at the destruction of the world. Others again, though they do not oppose these, nevertheless are unwilling to restrict it precisely to the final judgment, but contend that it must be extended to all times, from his first coming to the second, and also to that which is still to come, q) to the whole time of the gospel, in which he promises to protect his Church and destroy its enemies; of which, however many examples of this there are in this world, there will be more and clearer ones on the last day of things. The reverend r) Diodati has thought fit to gather these opinions in his notes on the preceding words, and he thinks all of them apply to these and the following words. And they wish this also to be explained partly figuratively, as of the divine vengeance which God took on the enemies of his people after their deliverance from the Babylonian captivity; but chiefly and spiritually it should be referred to the judgments which Christ executes on the enemies of the Church redeemed by him, and specifically it looks to the final and general deliverance at the second coming. But by what reasons these and other interpreters strive, drawn too far apart in different directions, and what must be decided about their diverse opinions, I think it will be more to the point to add, when we come to examine the words in detail, in the order in which they stand, to which task, with God's help, we now prepare ourselves after these general remarks.

units.la: v. 1. Quia ecce in diebus illis & in tempore illo, quo convertam captivitatem Jehuda & Hierosolyma.
units.tr: v. 1. For behold, in those days and at that time when I shall restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem.

units.la: 2. Ego

n) Et confulc Theodoret. o) Druf. p) Ribera. Christ. a Castro. Pet. a Fig. qui inquit Nostri fere referunt ad diem universalis judicii, quod plerique faciunt. q) Mer. Tarnov. r) Qui eadem hic cum Calvino sentire videtur.
units.tr: n) Consult also Theodoret. o) Drusius. p) Ribera, Christ. a Castro, Pet. a Fig., who says: "Our writers mostly refer this to the day of universal judgment, as most do." q) Mer., Tarnov. r) who seems to hold the same view as Calvin here.

units.la: 2. Ego congregabo etiam omnes gentes & faciam descendere eas in vallem Josaphat, & disceptabo cum eis pro populo meo & hareditate mea Israel, quos disperserunt in nationibus & terram meam diviserunt.
units.tr: 2. I will also gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will plead with them there for my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations and divided my land.

units.la: כִּי הִנֵּה Ci hinneh, Quia ecce. Particula כִּי nostrat. quia, uti diversis linguis in aliis versionibus per particulam hujus significationis exprimitur, Grotio rectius censetur verti, verum sive sed, (quem {s}) alii sequuntur) utpote quo melius connectantur hæc verba cum præcedentibus cap. 2. ubi innui putat quosdam eorum, qui effugerant, in captivitatem esse abductos, quibus hic promittatur liberatio. Non est certe qui dubitet, hanc particulam alibi significare sed; at non video, cur denotatio ejus, quia, hic non sit accommodata ad connectendum hæc verba cum præcedentibus, quippe quibus non obscure declaratur, quo tempore ac ubinam loci illorum residuorum liberatio juxta ac aliorum exitium futurum sit.
units.tr: Ci hinneh [כִּי הִנֵּה], For behold. The particle כִּי, which in our language is "quia" (because), is expressed in other versions in various languages by a particle of this same meaning. Grotius rightly holds that it should be rendered "but" or "yet" (a rendering others follow), since these words are thereby better connected with the preceding in chapter 2. There he thinks some of those who escaped were carried off into captivity, and here liberation is promised to them. No one doubts that this particle elsewhere means "but". Yet I do not see why its meaning "because" should not fit here to connect these words with what precedes, since it is clearly declared there at what time and in what place the liberation of those survivors, as well as the destruction of the others, is to take place.

units.la: הִנֵּה, Hinneh, ecce, particula, {t}) attentionis nota, quæ excitat ac simul confirmat, quamvis gravia videantur atque dubia, de quibus hic sermonem facit Propheta, attamen certo esse futura. In diebus illis & in tempore illo, quo convertam captivitatem Judæ & Hierosolymæ. Quibus simul indicat tempus olim fuisse, quo in captivitatem abducti erant, quorum hic ratio habetur, quod antea quamvis expressum non sit; tamen illis hic promissionem fieri, fore ut inde eripiantur, certum est. Judam & Hierosolymam, quo nomine ad literam notantur Judæi, captivam fuisse abductam monumenta historiarum non uno loco testantur. Abducebantur a Nebuchadnosore Babylonem, 2. Reg. 24, 14. &c. & in libertatem restituti sunt inde sub Cyro Persarum rege 2. Chron. 36, 22. 23. & Esra 1. quod tempus hic respici quorundam opinio est; at inficias id eunt alii, quia non possunt ostendere cætera etiam esse secuta, veluti gentium congregationem in valle {u}) Jehosaphat. Rursus captivi sunt redditi Romanis, post adventum Christi
units.tr: Hinneh [הִנֵּה], behold: a particle marking attention, which arouses and at the same time confirms that the matters the prophet here speaks of, however grave and doubtful they may seem, will certainly come to pass. In those days and at that time when I shall restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem. By these words he indicates that there was once a time when they were led into captivity, and that their case is taken into account here, though it was not expressed before. That a promise is made to them here, that they will be snatched from there, is certain. That Judah and Jerusalem, by which name the Jews are literally meant, were led away captive is attested by the records of history in more than one place. They were carried off by Nebuchadnezzar to Babylon (2 Kings 24:14, etc.), and were restored to liberty from there under Cyrus, king of the Persians (2 Chron. 36:22-23 and Ezra 1). Some think this time is what is here regarded; but others deny it, because they cannot show that the rest also followed, such as the gathering of the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat. Again, they were handed over to the Romans after the coming of Christ

units.la: {s}) Bren. Veil. {t}) Ar. Mont. Tarnov. {u}) Chr. a Castro. Christi sub Tito & aliis, unde in libertatem adhucdum non sunt vindicati, quod ιυ) futurum praestolantur in extremis temporibus, quibus hanc prophetiam putant impletum iri. Verum cum hujus rei praestolandae nulla sit ratio, alii Christianorum sunt, qui haec verba probe exponi posse exististimant non quidem ad literam de captivis Judaeis in civitatem suam restituendis, sed spiritualiter de iis in libertatem vindicandis, qui x) captivi sunt peccato & diabolo, jugoq; Mosaicae legis & Antichristi. Quo sensu si verba accipiantur, non tantum intelligendi sunt hic per Judam & Hierosolymam, (ut plerique volunt) Judaei, sed tota DEI ecclesia, quotquot & quicunque in eam admittuntur & colligentur non ex Judaeis tantum, verum & ex omnibus aliis gentibus, quibus ad Evangelicam veritatem vocatis haec nomina juxta linguam in S. literis usitatam egregie convenient, imo omnibus illis qui veritatem amplectuntur, quae prius praedicata est in Juda & Hierosolyma, unde eorum nomina postea sortiti sunt omnes, qui sunt y) domestici & cives z) novae (& verae) & sanctae Hierosolymae; quippe in Christo non amplius erat differentia inter a) Graecum & Judaeum, sed omnes idem videbantur in Christo Jesu, omnes sub ejus ecclesiae nomine comprehendebantur. Haut b) quibusdam ecclesia Dei his nominibus significetur, eodemque recurrat, sive Judam & Hierosolymam dicas, sive Ecclesiam. Hanc ob causam ita haec verba παροικία Reverendus Episcopus Hallius: In diebus Evangelii, quibus meam Ecclesiam restituam, & a spirituali captivitate liberabo, qua fuit afflicta. Qua ratione nec causa nec locus erit quaestioni, quam quidam Judaeorum hic nectunt, nimirum, quare non potius hic sit appellatus Israel, quo nomine concluduntur omnes tribus, quam Judah sive Hierosolyma, quae uni tribui tantum propria sunt, ac si ad eos solos promissio pertineret, cum in confesso sit ad caeteros eam quoque spectare. Huic solvendae adferunt quidam, id propterea factum esse, quia Joel in specie c) prophetiam habebat ad Judam & Hierosolymam, utpote quibus * peculiariter erat missus: alii (uti Kimchi) quia, Israelitae etsi omnes reditturi sunt, Messias erit ex tribu Juda, cujus propter-ea
units.tr: {s}) Brenz, Veil. {t}) Ar. Mont., Tarnov. {u}) Christ. a Castro. under Titus and others, whence they have not yet been freed, awaiting this as something to come in the last times, when they think this prophecy will be fulfilled. But since there is no reason to wait for this, others among the Christians think these words can be properly explained, not literally of Jewish captives restored to their city, but spiritually of those to be freed who are captive to sin and the devil, and to the yoke of the Mosaic law and of Antichrist. If the words are taken in this sense, then by Judah and Jerusalem are to be understood not merely the Jews (as most wish), but the whole Church of God, all and whoever are admitted and gathered into it, not only from the Jews but from all other nations. To these, when they are called to the evangelical truth, these names fit admirably according to the language customary in the Holy Scriptures. Indeed they apply to all who embrace the truth which was first preached in Judah and Jerusalem, from which all who are domestics and citizens of the new (and true) and holy Jerusalem afterwards received their names; for in Christ there was no longer any difference between Greek and Jew, but all seemed the same in Christ Jesus, all were comprehended under the name of his Church. It makes no difference whether the Church of God is signified by these names, and it comes to the same thing whether you say Judah and Jerusalem or the Church. For this reason the Reverend Bishop Hall paraphrases these words thus: "In the days of the Gospel, when I shall restore my Church and deliver her from the spiritual captivity by which she was afflicted." By this reasoning there is neither cause nor place for the question which some of the Jews raise here, namely why it is not called here "Israel", by which name all the tribes are included, rather than "Judah" or "Jerusalem", which belong only to one tribe, as if the promise pertained to them alone, when it is agreed that it also looks to the others. Some offer this solution: that it was done for this reason, because Joel had a prophecy specifically addressed to Judah and Jerusalem, to whom he had been peculiarly sent. Others (like Kimchi) say it is because, although all Israelites are to return, the Messiah will be of the tribe of Judah, on whose account

units.la: §§) Id. x) Tirin. y) Ephes. 2,19. z) Apoc. 3,12. & 21,2. & 10. a) Gal. 3,28. Col. 3,11. b) Pet. a Fig. c) Abarbinel. *) Pet. a Fig. ea in specie mentionem facit, sicut etiam Hierosolyma, quia erat �ork Rosh, caput civitatis sive regni, & quia ibi erit prælium Gog & Magog (quorum mentionem injecimus supra c. 1,31.) Verum si tam late patet illorum nominum significatio juxta stylum Novi Fœderis, hæc quæstio, ut diximus, locum non habebit. Juda & Hierosolyma complectitur Israelem quoque, idque non tantum qua denotat hanc gentem juxta carnem, sed omnes veros Israelitas DEI; omnes qui sunt fidei Abrahami, quamvis non ejus feminis. Omnes veri fideles, cujuscunque sint nationis, omnia membra d) cœlestis novæ Hierosolyma, Ecclesiæ Christi, cujus Juda & Hierosolyma olim erant imago & typus: omnes hi, inquam, possunt in hoc mundo dici peregrini & extranei, imo captivi, in quos, non secus agit cupiditas, quam infensissimus hostis. Adeo ut scire illis applicari possit, quod hic dicitur: quo convertam captivitatem Juda & Hierosolyma, quippe quibus omnes ad unum comprehenduntur. Promissum includit haud obscurum, quod dicitur, ego convertam &c. fore ut debito tempore, a se constituto, certissime efficiat, quod illis facturum sancte promiserat. Tempus illud non est præcise determinatum; ita ut egregie huc quadrent verba Salvatoris nostri, Matth. 24,36. Caterum illum diem atque horam nemo scit, sed Pater meus solus, adeo ut mirum non sit, interpretes eos, e) qui id determinant, tam longe a se invicem abire, ut vidimus, quos inter equidem tutissimum est eos sequi, qui id nullo certo spatio limitant, sed ita extendunt, ut non tantum id sub eo comprehendatur, quo DEus in peculiarem populum sibi vindicabat olim Judæos, sed & omne illud quod post Christi adventum labitur, quo captivos liberavit, adhuc liberat ac liberabit ad finem mundi usque redemptos tum ex Judæis, tum ex gentibus, f) a servitute interitus in gloriosam liberorum Dei libertatem, cum g) mors absorpta fuerit gloriose, nullique inimici amplius superstites fuerint, qui eos contineant in servitute sub potentia sua, vel h) divellant eos ab amore Dei, qui est in Christo Jesu & perenni præsentiæ ac gratiæ ejus perceptione. Hinc cum omnia hic facta promissa
units.tr: §§) Same. x) Tirinus. y) Eph. 2:19. z) Rev. 3:12, 21:2, 10. a) Gal. 3:28, Col. 3:11. b) Peter a Fig. c) Abarbanel. *) Peter a Fig. mentions it specifically, as also Jerusalem, because it was Rosh [ראש], the head of the city or kingdom, and because there the battle of Gog and Magog will take place (of which we made mention above, ch. 1:31). But if the meaning of those names extends so widely according to the style of the New Testament, this question, as we have said, will have no place. Judah and Jerusalem embrace Israel also, and that not only insofar as it denotes this nation according to the flesh, but all the true Israelites of God: all who are of the faith of Abraham, though not of his seed. All true believers, of whatever nation, all the members of the heavenly new Jerusalem, the Church of Christ, of which Judah and Jerusalem were once the image and type: all these, I say, can in this world be called pilgrims and strangers, indeed captives, whom greed treats no less than the most hostile enemy does. So that what is said here, "whither I shall restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem", can be applied to them, since all of them, one and all, are comprehended in those names. The promise includes nothing obscure in what is said, "I will restore", etc., namely that at the time he has appointed, he will most certainly bring about what he solemnly promised to do. That time is not precisely determined, so that the words of our Saviour fit admirably: "But of that day and hour no one knows, but my Father alone" (Matt. 24:36). It is therefore no wonder that the interpreters who fix it diverge so far from one another, as we have seen. Among them it is surely safest to follow those who limit it to no certain span, but extend it so that it is comprehended not only under that period in which God once claimed the Jews as his peculiar people, but also all that has passed since the coming of Christ, in which he has freed captives, still frees, and will free the redeemed up to the end of the world, both from the Jews and from the Gentiles, "from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God" (Rom. 8:21). This will be when death has been gloriously swallowed up (1 Cor. 15:54), and no enemies remain who might hold them in servitude under their power, or "separate them from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus" (Rom. 8:34), and from the perpetual presence and grace of him being perceived. Hence, since all the things promised here are yet to be fulfilled,

units.la: d) Heb. 12,22. vide D. Hammond. in h. l. ita & Apoc. 3,12. & 21,2. e) Sicut Calv. Diodati &c. f) Rom. 8,21. g) 1. Cor. 15,54. h) Rom. 8,34. tunc complenda sint, isque dies plenam redemtionem Judæ ac Hierosolymæ DEI dederit, i) quidam hæc verba, quo convertam captivitatem &c. ita exponit, cum completus fuerit prædestinatorum numerus, vel ut verbis Apostoli infigniter huc facientibus utamur: k) donec plenus & Judæorum & gentium intret numerus. Quapropter certo futurum est tale tempus, quo omnia hæc promissa bona his ejus electis, quibus jam ex parte hic fruuntur, abunde ac plene impertientur. Quod sicuti res est extra omnem dubitationis aleam constituta; ita non minus verum est, & illud instare tempus, quo omnes illos acerrime est ulturus, qui eos hucusque oppresserunt, id quod dilucide etiam sequentia docent verba: Ego congregabo etiam omnes gentes & faciam descendere eos in vallem Josaphat &c. Ut rite intelligamus, quid hæc verba sibi velint, & de interpretum expositionibus exploratius judicemus, necessarium erit omnium primo inquirere, quid hic sit vallis Josaphat, cujus alibi in S. literis nulla omnino fit mentio, præterquam hoc capite iterum v. 12. Quidam id habent pro loci nomine proprio; at cum alibi non memoretur, nec ejus hic accuratior distinctiorve detur descriptio, haud facile dictu est, quisnam fuerit. Alii, ut supra notatum est, l) eundem volunt cum eo, qui 2. Par. 20, 26. dicitur vallis Beracha (sive benedictionis) quia Domino benedicebat ibi Josaphat & ejus populus, propter insignem destructionem, qua DEO operante hostes cadebant, ex quo benedictionis postea illud nomen sortitus est locus. Kimchi arbitratur esse vallem Hierosolymæ propinquam, ita dictam propter monumentum a Jehoshaphat ibi erectum, aut propter opus quoddam insigne, quod ibi fecerat, unde ejus nomen ei esset impositum. Quod istud nomen illi valli inditum sit a sepulchro Josaphati in ea sito, ut quidam sentiunt, m) parum probabilitatis habet, eo quod 2. Paral. 21, 2. dicitur sepultus cum patribus suis in civitate Davidis, quorum sepulchra non nisi in monte Zionis intra civitatem fuerunt, nisi cum n) aliis statuere malimus, exuvias ejus inde erutas atque monumento esse inser-
units.tr: d) Heb. 12,22. See Dr Hammond on this place; so also Apoc. 3,12 and 21,2. e) As Calvin, Diodati, etc. f) Rom. 8,21. g) 1 Cor. 15,54. h) Rom. 8,34. When these things promised here are to be fulfilled, and that day shall have given Judah and Jerusalem of God full redemption, i) some explain these words, I will bring back their captivity, etc., as meaning when the number of the predestined is completed; or, to use the words of the Apostle, which bear strongly on this point, k) until the full number of Jews and Gentiles comes in. Therefore there will certainly be a time when all these promised blessings will be bestowed abundantly and fully on those elect of his who now enjoy them in part here. Since this is established beyond every chance of doubt, it is no less true that the time is at hand when he will most sharply avenge all those who have oppressed them until now, as the following words also clearly teach: I will gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, etc. So that we may rightly understand what these words mean, and judge more carefully the interpreters' explanations, we must first inquire what the valley of Jehoshaphat is here. Nowhere else in Holy Scripture is there any mention of it, except again in this chapter at v. 12. Some take it as a proper place-name; but since it is not mentioned elsewhere, and no more exact or distinct description of it is given here, it is not easy to say what it was. Others, as noted above, l) wish it to be the same as the place which 2 Chron. 20,26 calls the valley of Berachah (that is, of blessing), because Jehoshaphat and his people blessed the Lord there, on account of the notable destruction in which, by God's working, the enemies fell; and from this the place afterwards received that name of blessing. Kimchi thinks it is the valley near Jerusalem, so called on account of a monument erected there by Jehoshaphat, or on account of some notable work he had done there, from which it received its name. That this name was given to the valley from the tomb of Jehoshaphat situated in it, as some think, m) has little probability, because 2 Chron. 21,2 says he was buried with his fathers in the city of David, whose tombs were only in Mount Zion within the city; unless we prefer, with n) others, to hold that his remains were dug up from there and placed in a monument erected to his memory there.

Livel. {m} Livel. {n} Ribera, Menoch. infertas in memoriam ipsius ibi erecto. Hanc vallem q) alii constituunt inter Hierosolymam & montem olivarum, quam eandem nonnulli dicunt vocatam esse Cedron.
units.tr: {i} Pet. a Fig. {k} Rom. 11,25, compared with Eph. 1,9-10: In the dispensation of the fullness of times he will restore all things which he has set in himself. {l} Galv. Jun. Trem. Livel. {m} Livel. {n} Ribera, Menoch. placed in a monument erected there to his memory. Others place this valley between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives, and some say that this same valley was called Kidron.

units.la: Quantumvis hi immane quantum differant quia situm ac rationem huius nominis, in eo tamen hactenus conveniunt, loci nomen proprium esse. At alii aliter sentiunt, quippe hac denominatione tantum alludi statuunt ad quendam forte ita dictum locum, & ad id quod ibi gestum erat; vocem autem revera significare p) judicium Domini, atque talem denotare q) locum, ubi judicium suum Dominus exercebit in hostes Ecclesiae. Hinc est ut in eo cum dissentiant, non major illorum consensus sit in ceteris, quidnam DEus ibi sit facturus, quod judicium exerciturus; item quinam sint illi judicandi, quorum hic mentio fit nomine omnium gentium. Ex iis enim magna illa enascitur differentia, quam memoravimus in prolegomenis huius capitis, quae non aliunde originem trahit, quam quod tam diversi sint in exponenda valle Josaphat. Etenim cum sint, qui proprii nominis loco id habeant, uti diximus, illi hic innui sibi persuadent illam cladem ingentis multitudinis diversarum gentium, quae invadebant Judam tempore Josaphat 2. Reg. 20. quae opinio his verbis plane non videtur convenire, tum r) quia gentes hic nominatae, puta Moabitae & Ammonitae & montani Seiris (sive Idumaei) proprie non dici possunt omnes gentes: tum quia haec res, uti observavimus, non facile congruere potest tempori huius prophetiae, qua quaedam dicuntur potius futura, quam antea facta.
units.tr: However much these authors differ enormously about the site and nature of this name, they agree so far in this, that it is a proper place-name. Others think otherwise, holding that the name alludes only to some place perhaps so called, and to what happened there; and that the word really means p) the judgment of the Lord, and denotes q) the place where the Lord will execute his judgment on the enemies of the Church. Hence, although they disagree on this point, there is no greater agreement among them on the rest: what God will do there, what judgment he will execute; and likewise who are the ones to be judged, named here by the term all the nations. From these questions arises that great difference which we mentioned in the prolegomena to this chapter, and it springs from nothing else than that they differ so much in explaining the valley of Jehoshaphat. For since some take it as a proper name, as we have said, they persuade themselves that what is meant here is that slaughter of a huge multitude of various nations which invaded Judah in the time of Jehoshaphat, 2 Kings 20. This opinion does not seem to agree plainly with these words: first, because the nations named here, namely the Moabites, Ammonites, and the mountain people of Seir (that is, the Edomites), cannot properly be called all nations; second, because, as we have observed, this event cannot easily fit the time of this prophecy, in which certain things are said to be future rather than already done.

units.la: Eadem ratione loci nititur opinio, quam sequitur Kimchi, omnibus nationibus denotari eos, qui venturi sint cum Gog & Magog adversus Hierosolymam atque superandi in valle sic dicta; quae opinio, qua quid postea complendum sit statuitur, tam improbabilis est, quam certum, id nondum esse factum. Pari fundamento fulcitur sententia Cyrilli, qui id de clade hostium intelligit Judaeorum post reditum ex Babylone, qui impedimento forent illis in aedificanda Hierosolyma: Nam etsi in ea historia nulla injicitur mentio vallis Jehoshaphat; attamen-
units.tr: On the same ground of place rests the opinion which Kimchi follows, that by all nations are meant those who will come with Gog and Magog against Jerusalem and be overcome in the valley so called. This opinion, which holds that something is still to be fulfilled, is as improbable as it is certain that this has not yet happened. The view of Cyril rests on an equally weak foundation: he understands it of the slaughter of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon, who were hindrances to them in rebuilding Jerusalem. For although no mention of the valley of Jehoshaphat is made in that history, nevertheless

units.la: e) Lyra. vid. Livel. p) Ita ex Judaeis Abarb. q) Mercer. r) Drusius. men dicit quod sit αραχδόσεως λόγος, traditione acceptum. At non video, quomodo probare possit, tum, quod ab eo dictum est, manifestum esse in S. literis, tum quod hic scriptum extat, jamjam esse completum. Alia praeterea est, quae multo latius sese diffudit, quae statuunt hanc vallem esse loci proprium, atque ex eo, quod hocce modo sit constituta & descripta, argumentum evadere, omnes ultimo judicii universalis die, qui unquam vixissent & suscitati essent, (uti certo tunc erunt) congregatum iri in hunc locum, nimirum in Vallem Josaphat, ut coram DEO ibi appareant sententias audituri. Meminit hujus opinionis Cyrillus quasi perquam vulgatae inter Judaeos, majoris autem non habetur ab eo, quam ὑθλῳ σαπρὸς καὶ γεγωδης, mere nugatoria ac frivola & anilis fabula. Cujus momenti & auctoritatis ea fuerit ejus tempore, vel postea inter Judaeos, non reperio; at s) certum est, eam pervulgatam fuisse recentiori seculo inter Christianos, unde a quibusdam etiam rejicitur, veluti t) figmentum aut u) pueriliter dictum, ob eam inter caeteras rationem, w) quod haec vallis sit nimis angusta, quam ut possit simul omnes, quae ab initio mundi vixerunt, gentes capere. Verum non est tam obsoleta, quin ejus rationem adhuc habeant x) alii autumantes, Christum habiturum esse revera ibi folium suum in aere omnesque in ea & circa eam collectum atque ab eo judicatum iri, quod confirmare conantur ex Act. 1, 11. Hic Jesus, qui in coelum receptus est, sic veniet, quo pacto vidistis eum in coelum ascendentem. Quod tantundem valere existimant, ac si eodem loco, unde assumtus est in coelum, iterum sit descensurus eoque collecturus ac judicaturus omnes gentes, quem nullum volunt alium quam y) vallem Jehoshaphat. Ubi, inquiunt, z) docebat, ubi ipse erat justificatus, ibi probabile est eum esse rursus descensurum ad judicandum. At quicquid illi hanc in rem proferunt, sibi ipsis tantum est 4) probabile; quippe manifestum est, hunc locum ex Actis citatum magis respicere & explicare b) modum redeundi, quam locum. Nullum praeterea adducunt firmum argumentum, quo verum
units.tr: e) Lyra. See Livel. p) So Abarbanel among the Jews. q) Mercer. r) Drusius. he says it is a saying received by tradition [ἀπὸ παραδόσεως λόγος]. But I do not see how he can prove either that what he says is plain in Holy Scripture, or that what is written here is already fulfilled. There is also another view, which has spread much more widely: it holds that this valley is a real place, and from the fact that it has been fixed and described in this way, it draws the argument that all who have ever lived and been raised up (as they certainly will be then) will be gathered into this place on the last day of universal judgment, namely into the Valley of Jehoshaphat, to appear there before God and hear their sentences. Cyril mentions this opinion as very widespread among the Jews, but he does not esteem it more highly than ὕθλος σαπρὸς καὶ γεγωδης [a rotten and senile idle tale], a mere trifling, frivolous and old-wives' fable. What weight and authority it had in his time, or later among the Jews, I do not find; but it is certain that it was very widely accepted among Christians in a later age, and for that reason some reject it, calling it a fiction or speaking of it as childish, chiefly because, among other reasons, this valley is too narrow to hold at once all the nations that have lived since the beginning of the world. Yet it is not so obsolete that others do not still take account of it, claiming that Christ will in fact have his throne there in the air, and that all will be gathered in it and around it and judged by him; they try to confirm this from Acts 1,11: This Jesus, who was taken up into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go up into heaven. They think this means as much as if he would descend again to the very place from which he was taken up into heaven, and there gather and judge all the nations; and they will allow no other place than the valley of Jehoshaphat. Where, they say, he was taught, where he was justified, there it is probable he will descend again to judge. But whatever these men bring forward on this matter is probable only to themselves; for it is plain that the passage from Acts cited here concerns rather the manner of his return than the place. Moreover, they adduce no firm argument by which the truth

units.la: 1) Sic Lyra & alii multi. r) Calv. u) Mercer. 66) Tarnov. x) Ribera & alii non pauci, qui in eo praecipuum scholasticum sequuntur. y) Vatablus de quibusdam, & Mariana in Tarnov. z) Sa Tirin. 4) Pet. a Fig. & Sa. b) Tarnov. rum esse evincant, Christum judicaturum esse ultimo die in ea valle; id quod & de aliis dicendum est, qui alteram sententiam tuentur, qua id loci nomen esse, uti notavimus, probare volunt. Rectius itaque ac melius sibi videntur facere alii, qui appellative hoc nomen accipiunt, ut non denotet illud, quod hic memoratur esse futurum in hoc loco, sed, quod alibi postea fieret, non absimile fore quadantenus ei, quod hoc loco aliquando erat factum, eoque locum illum vocari nomine illius, qui hujus erat typus, eamque nominis communicationem justa fieri ex ratione. Atque hac ratione si quando accipiunt verba vel appellative, ut idem valeant ac si dictum esset, Deus judicabit, vel judicium Dei, uti Chaldaeus reddit משור פלוג vallem divisionis (sive distributionis) judicii, vel alias pro loco, qui respectu rerum efficiendarum cum referret locum, qui nomine vallis Iosaphat cognitus erat, non opus erit ad eum locum id restringere, qui olim ita erat appellatus, sed talem intelligere locum, qualiscunque demum is fit, ubi eo, quo hic traditur, modo DEus judicium fit certo certius executurus tempore ac loco sibi praefixo ac constituto. Quod ad tempus attinet, ea hic iterum est inter interpretes differentia, cujus antea meminimus, quorum quidam id in specie magis ad ultimi judicii diem referunt, alii ad omnia Evangelii tempora ab adventu Christi primo ad secundum usque. Qui tamen meo judicio perquam facile conciliari possunt, quippe illi, qui ad omnia tempora hoc referunt, ultimum diem magnum diem DEI habent (quem quidam innui putant, quando nomini DEI adjungitur judicium) quo dubio procul quam maxime fient, quae hic praedicuntur; illi vero, qui cumprimis ad hunc diem respici existimant, nequaquam excludunt, quod aliquando ante id tempus futurum est DEO graviter animadvertente judiciis suis in hostes ecclesiae. Quod ad locum, quamvis, qui ultimae sententiae addicti sunt, non concedant hoc esse proprium nomen alicujus peculiaris loci hoc nomine celebris; attamen ad aliquem arbitrantur alludi talem locum & hujusmodi circumstantias, quae cum eo sunt conjunctae. Si ad eam alludatur convallem, in qua illi inimici, qui contra Iosaphat arma capiebant, (2. Paral. 20.) tam miran-
units.tr: 1) So Lyra and many others. r) Calvin. u) Mercer. 66) Tarnovius. x) Ribera and not a few others, who in this follow the chief of the Schoolmen. y) Vatablus on some points, and Mariana in Tarnovius. z) Sa, Tirinus. 4) Pet. a Fig. and Sa. b) Tarnovius. They do not establish that Christ will judge on the last day in that valley. The same must be said of others who defend the other opinion, by which they want the name to be a place name, as we have noted. Others seem to act more rightly and better when they take this name as a common noun, so that it does not denote the place where the judgment is said here to take place in the future, but something that would happen elsewhere later, somewhat similar to what had once taken place in this place, and that this place is called by the name of the one who was its type, and that this sharing of the name is made for a just reason. If they take the words in this way as common nouns, so that they mean the same as if it had been said, God will judge, or the judgment of God, as the Chaldee paraphrast renders מישור פלוג [mishor peleg], the valley of division (or distribution) of judgment, or otherwise as a place which, with respect to the things to be done, relates to a place known by the name valley of Jehoshaphat, then there will be no need to restrict it to the place that was once so named, but to understand whatever place it may be, where God will execute judgment in the manner described here, most certainly at the time and place appointed and fixed by himself. As for the time, there is again the difference among the interpreters that we mentioned earlier: some refer it more particularly to the day of the last judgment, others to all the times of the Gospel from the first coming of Christ to the second. Yet in my judgment these can be reconciled very easily. For those who refer it to all the times hold that the last day is the great day of God (which some think is hinted at when judgment is joined to the name of God), on which, beyond doubt, the things foretold here will be fulfilled most fully; and those who think that this day is especially in view by no means exclude that something will happen before that time, as God severely punishes the enemies of the Church by his judgments.

units.la: e) Mers. d) Calv. e) Tarnov.
units.tr: e) Mersenne. d) Calvin. e) Tarnovius.

units.la: mirandum in modum sunt fusi clade insigni affecti, nihil aliud haec loci denominatione innui nonnulli volunt, quam ut in mentem revocetur ecclesiae DEI haec liberatio, quae eo tempore facta est, ut certissime sibi persuadeat, DEum eodem modo esse acturum in Ecclesiae defensionem atque vindictam sumturum de ejus hostibus. 2. Si nomine hujus vallis, quatenus non procul sita erat ab Hierosolyma, designetur locus a DEO constitutus ad exequendum illud, quod hic praedictum est, alii existimant hoc nomine indicari, quemadmodum DEus palam profligabat populi sui hostes in conspectu illorum, ita eum & praestituto tempore palam f) in conspectu ecclesiae executurum esse judicia in hostes ejus, ita ut juxta illos in valle Jehosaphat tantundem fit, ac in conspectu ecclesiae. Cur iste locus, ubi id facere constituit, vocetur vallis, haud ratione vacare non nullis persuasum est. Inter Judaeos est Abarbinel, qui ob profunditatem judiciorum DEI ita vocari putat, quorum manifestandorum hic constituitur locus ejus sunt profunda, ideo illum vocat locum, qui est (& ut ille ait vel ipsa significatione judicium DEI innuit) vallis Jehosaphat, quo etiam facit quod ante illum R. Sal. Jarchi tradit haec verba ita exponens Descendam cum illis in profunditatem judicii, quibus verbis, g) inquit, non nemo intelligit exactissimam judicium etiam de occultissimis.
units.tr: they were overwhelmed in a remarkable defeat and scattered in a marvellous manner. Some want the name of this place to suggest nothing else than that this deliverance of the Church of God, which was accomplished at that time, be brought back to mind, so that the Church may be fully assured that God will act in the same way in defence of his Church and take vengeance on her enemies. 2. If by the name of this valley, insofar as it lay not far from Jerusalem, a place appointed by God for carrying out what is foretold here is designated, others think that by this name is indicated that just as God openly routed the enemies of his people before their eyes, so at the appointed time he will openly execute his judgments on his enemies before the eyes of the Church, so that according to them what happens in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the same as what happens in the sight of the Church. Why this place, where he has determined to do this, is called a valley, some have been persuaded, is not without reason. Among the Jews there is Abarbanel, who thinks it is so called because of the depth of the judgments of God, whose revelation is appointed for this place: they are deep, therefore he calls the place which is (and, as he says, the very meaning of the word judgment of God suggests) the valley of Jehoshaphat. To this also belongs what R. Solomon Jarchi, before him, teaches, explaining these words thus: I will go down with them into the depth of judgment; by these words, he says, someone understands the most exact judgment, even on the most hidden things.

units.la: Quod si alios interpretes consulere volupe sit, has in caeteris, nisi fallor, suggerunt rationes, h) quia ibi tam obsessi erunt & circumdati, ut nullus effugio futurus sit locus i). 2. Quia eo necessitatis erunt compulsi ob conscientiae angorem propter peccata admissa, ut similes censeri possint illis, qui magna copia in angusta & incommoda valle, ubi non satis spatii est, premuntur. 3. Grotius depingi hic arbitratur judicia divina, quatenus DEus judex sedet in loco sublimi, rei stant in loco inferiori, qui vallis ob similitudinem hic dicitur.
units.tr: If you wish to consult other interpreters, they suggest, unless I am mistaken, these reasons among others: (1) because there the enemies will be so beset and surrounded that there will be no place of escape; (2) because they will be driven by necessity, on account of the anguish of conscience over sins committed, so that they may be considered like those who, in great numbers, are pressed together in a narrow and inconvenient valley where there is not enough room; (3) Grotius thinks that the divine judgments are depicted here, insofar as God the judge sits in a high place while the accused stand in a lower place, which is called a valley here because of the likeness.

units.la: Hactenus quod attinet ad nomen loci; sequitur in verbis sequentibus, quid DEus ibi facturus sit. Verba ita habent: Congregabo omnes
units.tr: So far as concerns the name of the place. There follows, in the words that come next, what God will do there. The words run thus: I will gather all

units.la: f) Jun. Trem. Pisc. Glass. Episcop. Hallius. g) Pet. a Fig. h) Tarn. i) More. omnes gentes, & faciam descendere eas ad vallem Josaphat, & disceptabo cum illis &c. Vix secus fieri potest, quin ex diversa interpretatione temporis & loci a DEO constitutorum ad ea exsequenda, quae hic dicuntur, nec non personarum, in quarum conspectu ea est executurus, differens etiam nascatur interpretum sententia de personis, quibus haec eventura dicuntur, nimirum uti hic describuntur, de omnibus gentibus, quae non eadem notione omnibus exponi possunt illis, qui adeo differunt in explicando tempore & loco. Si verba exponantur de tempore, quo Judaei a captivitate sunt restituti ac in libertatem quovis modo recuperatam vindicati, necesse est ut de talibus etiam accipiatur hostibus, qui hoc modo cum illis egerunt vel aggressi sunt eos ad exitium illis parandum, quique eandem ob causam a DEO atrociter essent castigati, ita ut omnes gentes non denotaret omnes universaliter, sed magnam copiam diversarum gentium, uti k) Assyriorum, Chaldaeorum & aliorum, qui cum illis advenerant odio Judaeorum & eorum l) religionis, quae tunc temporis vera erat sola, ob quam tum m) exosi erant Judaei omnibus aliis idololatricis gentibus. Rursus, si de tempore Evangelii, iisque omnibus intervallis, quae praeterlapsa sunt ac praeterlabuntur a primo Christi adventu ad secundum usque, manifestum quoque est, non significari omnes nationes sine ulla alicujus exceptione; sed omnes inter illas, sive Judaeos sive Gentiles, cujuscunque generis, qui ecclesiae DEI ac verae religionis Christianae sunt n) hostes, & in quos propter ignominiam, qua Ecclesiam DEI affecerunt, severe animadversum est, veluti in Judaeos, cum civitas eorum destrueretur tota republica funditus eversa, atque sic omnes nationes hic dicuntur, qui alias Matth. 13,14. describuntur omnia offendicula & omnes facientes iniquitatem. Quod si autem ad tempora adventus Christi secundi pertineant & ad ultimum judicium, nemini dubium esse potest, quin verba in maxima latitudine & strictissima significatione sumta sint verissima. Cum enim venerit Filius hominis cum sua gloria, nec non omnes sancti Angeli
units.tr: f) Junius, Tremellius, Piscator, Glassius, Bishop Hall. g) Pet. a Fig. h) Tarnovius. i) More. all nations, and will bring them down to the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them, etc. It can hardly happen otherwise than that, from the differing interpretation of the time and place appointed by God for carrying out the things said here, and also of the persons before whose eyes he will execute them, there also arises a difference of opinion among the interpreters about the persons to whom these things are said to happen. Namely, as they are described here, all nations, which cannot be explained in the same sense by all those who differ so much in explaining the time and place. If the words are explained of the time when the Jews were restored from captivity and vindicated into liberty recovered in any way, it is necessary that they be taken also of those enemies who dealt with them in this way or attacked them to prepare their ruin, and who for this same cause were severely punished by God; so that all nations would not denote all universally, but a great number of various nations, such as the k) Assyrians, Chaldeans and others who had come with them out of hatred of the Jews and of their l) religion, which at that time was alone true, and for which the Jews were then m) hated by all other idolatrous nations. Again, if it is concerned with the time of the Gospel, and with all those intervals which have passed and will pass from the first coming of Christ to the second, it is also clear that not all nations without any exception are signified; but all among them, whether Jews or Gentiles, of whatever kind, who are n) enemies of the Church of God and of the true Christian religion, and against whom severe vengeance has been taken on account of the outrage with which they treated the Church of God, as against the Jews when their city was destroyed, the whole commonwealth utterly overthrown; and thus all nations are here said, who are elsewhere described in Matthew 13 as all offences and all who work iniquity. But if they pertain to the times of the second coming of Christ and to the last judgment, no one can doubt that the words, taken in their widest extent and strictest meaning, are most true. For when the Son of Man comes in his glory, together with all the holy angels

units.la: k) Druf. l) Grot. m) Tarn. n) Hostes ecclesiae intelligit vel Judaeos vel gentes &c. quorum Judaei in vallem Jehosaphat possunt dici delati, cum civitas & status eorum destrueretur; gentes aliae autem, cum aliquando sint eversae. Merc. geli cum eo, tum sedebit in throno gloria sua, & coram eo congregabuntur omnes gentes & separabit eos alios ab aliis, quemadmodum separat pastor oves ab hædis &c. Matth. 25, 31. 32. &c. Omnes ex omnibus nationibus, probi atque improbi, verbis latissima significatione acceptis, colligentur coram eo. Verum quod hoc loco, si ad illud temporis intervallum referatur, non sint tam late accipienda, sed verius restringenda ad improbos eorum, non ad vera Ecclesiæ membra, sed ad hostes ejus, ex verbis apparet, quæ cum his sunt conjuncta, quibus describitur, quem in finem sint congregandi & quomodo DEus cum illis sit acturus. Faciet eos descendere in locum judicii & disceptabit cum eis ibi de populo suo &c. והורדתים Et faciam eos descendere, vel efficiam ut descendant; expressio naturæ rei apte conveniens, quippe locus vocatur vallis, quo, qui ex aliis locis veniunt, descendunt, quamvis eadem res, cum duodecimo versu exhibetur, voce contrariæ significationis dicatur, ascendere ad vallem Iosaphat, ut in proprio ejus loco, DEO volente, videbimus: De quo loquendi genere, quod in præsentiarum notandum habemus, eo tendit, verba hic descendere, ibi ascendere contrariæ quidem notionis, eandem tamen rem denotantia, non stricte esse accipienda de diverso veniendi modo ad præstitutum locum, sed potius de certitudine ac necessitate veniendi, ut ascendant vel descendant eo, undecunque locorum citarentur, quo ubi venerint, vel rectius, ubi convenerint, inquit ille, disceptabit cum illis ibi de suo populo &c. ונשפטתי עמם שם Venishpatti immam sham: Disceptabo cum illis ibi. Contendet cum illis jure, sicuti quis, quo injuria est affectus, eum in jus vocat, ac cum eo contendit, a quo læsus est; non quidem ut judex, ad quem rerum nihil pertinet, quique ad querelam personæ læsæ sententiam solet pronuntiare contra eum, qui injuria affecit; sed uti quis, qui simul injuria, qua pars læsa est affecta, afficitur & injuriarum est particeps; atque disceptabit non secus ac si propria ipsius res ageretur. Id enim videtur inferre verbum נשפטתי Nishpatti ea forma, qua hic & alibi usurpatur. Alii id exponunt conjugatione prima שפט Shaphatti p) judicio publico damnatos puniam, quasi judicis partem ageret, non autem Pet. a Fig. Pisc. Judicabo, judicium exercebo. Pet. a Fig. autem ullius partis, & se ipsum ita exhiberet, ut v. 12. ait: Ego sedebo ad judicandum omnes gentes. Attamen usitatius est ea conjugatione, qua hic est, atque a nostratibus & aliis exprimitur per q) disceptare cum & contendere in judicio tanquam pars laesa, qua quoque r) majorem videtur habere emphalin, utpote communionem ac relationem referens, quae intercedit inter DEum & populum suum. Ita ut ad se pertinere velit, quicquid ei contingat ejusque causam non secus ac suam ipsius agat, juxta id quod alibi dicit: Qui tangit vos, tangit pupillam oculi mei, Zach. 2,8. Quod horum cui factum, mihi factum est, Matth. 25,45. Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? dicit Christus Paulo ecclesiam ejus persequenti, Act. 9,4. Quanta sit ea propinquitas, qua sibi suos asserit & cognoscit eos, quorum loco disceptaturus est cum omnibus illorum hostibus, non obscure innuitur illis titulis, quibus insigniuntur, videlicet populi mei & hereditatis meae, Israelis. Quam invisi vero essent caeteris gentibus, quantaveque ignominia ac dedecore exceptis, tanquam ipsissima terrae purgamenta, & quorum nulla habenda cura & ratio, sequentia docent verba. Eos tamen nihilominus vocat suum populum & suam hereditatem, quorum habebat peculiarem curam ac rationem. Quantumvis enim eos permittat interdum potestati gravique persecutioni inimicorum suorum pariter atque illorum, idque vel in paternam castigationem ob admissa peccata, vel ad probandum eorum sinceritatem, vel ut palam illis fiat, mercedem magnam, quam praestolantur, non consistere in abundanti & tranquillo usu rerum temporalium hujus mundi, sed in rebus multo melioribus, quae sunt spirituales & ad meliorem vitam spectant; attamen id nequaquam indicium est, eos ab eo esse rejectos, quippe sibi illos adhuc venditat tanquam suum populum, suam hereditatem, a cujus jure nunquam decedet, utpote qui omnem injuriam illis illatam suam censet suoque tempore in conspectu illorum justitiam exercebit in eos, qui injuria illos affecerunt. Quae res uti eos potest servare, ne languescat & animum demittant gravissima anxietate pressi;
units.tr: k) Druf. l) Grot. m) Tarn. n) The enemies of the Church are understood to be either the Jews or the Gentiles, etc. Of these, the Jews can be said to be brought down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, when their city and state were destroyed; other nations, however, [can be said so] since at times they have been overthrown. Merc. "Then with him, and his glory, the Son of man shall sit on the throne, and before him shall be gathered all nations, and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides the sheep from the goats," etc. Matt. 25:31-32, etc. All men from all nations, good and bad, will be gathered before him, taking the words in their widest sense. But that these words should not be taken so broadly here, if they are referred to that interval of time, but should rather be restricted to the wicked among them, not to the true members of the Church but to its enemies, appears from the words which are joined to these and which describe for what end they are to be gathered and how God will deal with them. "I will bring them down" into the place of judgment, and "I will plead with them there concerning my people," etc. [והורדתים] "And I will bring them down," or "I will cause them to go down": an expression fitting the nature of the thing, since the place is called a valley, to which those who come from other places go down. Yet the same thing, when it is set forth in the twelfth verse, is expressed by a word of the opposite meaning, "to come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat," as we shall see in its proper place, God willing. Concerning this manner of speaking, which we should note for the present, the point is this: the words "to go down" here and "to come up" there, though of opposite meaning, denote the same thing, and are not to be taken strictly of a different way of coming to the appointed place, but rather of the certainty and necessity of coming, so that they go up or go down thither from whatever parts of the earth they are summoned; and when they have come, or more correctly, when they have gathered, he says, "I will plead with them there concerning my people," etc. [ונשפטתי עמם שם] "I will plead with them there." He will contend with them by right, as one who has been wronged summons the wrongdoer to law and contends with him by whom he was injured; not indeed as a judge, to whom the matter does not pertain, and who is accustomed to pronounce sentence against the wrongdoer at the complaint of the injured person; but as one who, at the same time, is affected by the wrong by which the injured party has been affected, and shares in the injuries; and he will plead just as if his own cause were being pleaded. For this seems to be implied by the verb [נשפטתי] "nishpatti" in the form in which it is used here and elsewhere. Others explain it by the first conjugation, [שפט] "shaphatti," "I will punish those condemned by public judgment," as if he were acting the part of a judge, and not [as] Pet. a Fig. Pisc. "I will judge, I will exercise judgment." But Pet. a Fig. does not [take] the part of any party, and does not present himself as he says in verse 12: "I will sit to judge all nations." Yet the conjugation used here is more customary, and is expressed by our countrymen and others by "to plead with" and "to contend in judgment" as the injured party, which also seems to have a greater emphasis, since it refers to the fellowship and relation that exists between God and his people; so that he wishes whatever happens to them to pertain to himself, and he acts in their cause no differently than in his own, according to what he says elsewhere: "He who touches you touches the apple of my eye," Zech. 2:8. "Inasmuch as you did it to one of these least of my brethren, you did it to me," Matt. 25:45. "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" says Christ to Paul persecuting his Church, Acts 9:4. How great is the nearness by which he claims and acknowledges as his own those in whose place he is about to plead with all their enemies, is not obscurely hinted by the titles with which they are marked, namely "my people" and "my inheritance, Israel." How hateful they would be to the other nations, and with what disgrace and dishonour they were received, as the very refuse of the earth, of whom no care or account is to be taken, the following words teach. Nevertheless he calls them "his people" and "his inheritance," for whom he had a particular care and regard. For although he sometimes allows them to be delivered to the power and heavy persecution of their enemies, as well as those others, either as a fatherly chastisement for sins committed, or to prove their sincerity, or so that it may be made plain to them that the great reward which they await does not consist in an abundant and tranquil use of the temporal things of this world, but in far better things, which are spiritual and look to a better life; yet this is by no means a sign that they have been rejected by him, for he still holds them out as his people, his inheritance, from whose right he will never depart, since he considers every injury done to them as done to himself, and in due time he will execute justice before their eyes upon those who have wronged them. This fact can keep them from fainting, lest, pressed by the most grievous anxiety, they lose heart;

units.la: q) דכן ingrediar in judicium cum. Kimchi. r) Vide Calv. prefli; ita argumento est,improborum potentiam,cui aliquando fuccumbit in hoc orbe populus DEI, non esse signum, quod magis sint accepti DEO, vel quod illorum actiones DEO probentur, licet inpræsentiarum eos sinat potentia crescere, eamque ratam habeat ob rationes, quas ipse optime novit,quibusque ductus omnia in bonum diriget illis, qui nunc sunt afflicti & persecutionem patiuntur. Id quod suo tempore certo fiet, quando disceptaturus est cum alteris pro alteris. Cum eos vocat suam hæreditatem, dilucide ostendit se nunquam eos aliquo modo esse relicturum, aut permissurum ut pereant,sed se vindicaturum sibi eos in æternum. Quam efficax sit hic titulus ad eum exorandum,ut curam illorum habeat,omniaque in illorum usum ac bonum dirigat, ex eo constat, quod cap.2.v.17. illis suggeritur,ubi precibus a DEO debebant impetrare,ut illis parceret, quia sint populus ejus, & non daret in opprobrium, quia sint hæreditas ejus.
units.tr: q) [דכן] "I will enter into judgment with," Kimchi. r) See Calvin. Thus it is an argument that the power of the wicked, to which the people of God sometimes give way in this world, is no sign that they are more acceptable to God, or that their actions are approved by God, even though for the present he lets their power grow and holds it fixed for reasons which he himself knows best, and by which, though he guides all things to the good of those who are now afflicted and suffer persecution. This will certainly come to pass in its own time, when he will plead with the others on behalf of the others. When he calls them "his inheritance," he clearly shows that he will never in any way abandon them or allow them to perish, but will claim them for himself forever. How effective this title is for moving him to take care of them and to direct all things to their use and good, is clear from the fact that in chapter 2, verse 17, it is suggested to them that they should obtain from God by prayer that he spare them, because they are "his people," and that he not give them "to reproach," because they are "his inheritance."
